## P2 - Podman log lines are written without newline separators in `WriteContainerLogs`

**Location:** [runtime/podman/podman.go:770-789](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/97a0b3b5da1ea93d0585c77987345c2adba9f81b/runtime/podman/podman.go#L770-L789)

**Problem:** `PodmanRuntime.WriteContainerLogs` writes each item received from the bindings&#39; `stdoutCh`/`stderrCh` with `io.WriteString(stdout, line)` and no separator. The Podman bindings&#39; `containers.Logs` sends one line per channel send without the trailing newline &#40;the response is read with `bufio.Scanner`, which strips it; the podman CLI re-adds the newline when printing these channels&#41;. The Docker implementation added in this PR does not share the issue because the Docker API returns the raw stream including newlines.

**Trigger:** Running `containerlab --runtime podman logs ...` on any lab. With multiple log lines, the whole log &#40;or the whole follow output&#41; is emitted as one concatenated line.

**Impact:** User-visible output corruption on a primary command path. Nothing catches it&#58; [`tests/01-smoke/32-logs.robot`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/97a0b3b5da1ea93d0585c77987345c2adba9f81b/tests/01-smoke/32-logs.robot#L1-L1) runs with `--runtime docker`, and even under the podman job its `--tail 1` assertion yields exactly one line either way; podman jobs are also `continue-on-error`.

**Suggested correction:** Append the newline at both write sites, for example `io.WriteString(stdout, line+"\n")`, and verify with one `podman logs` run. Consider a `--tail 2` line-count assertion in [`32-logs.robot`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/97a0b3b5da1ea93d0585c77987345c2adba9f81b/tests/01-smoke/32-logs.robot#L1-L1) once the suite is wired into CI.


## P3 - Port-forward error stream is closed immediately, so dial failures cannot reach the client

**Location:** [labruntime/clabernetes/access.go:383-413](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/97a0b3b5da1ea93d0585c77987345c2adba9f81b/labruntime/clabernetes/access.go#L383-L413)

**Problem:** `newPortForwardConn` closes the error stream right after creating it &#40;comment&#58; `the client sends nothing on the error stream`&#41; and then reads dial-failure messages from that same stream &#40;`io.ReadAll(errorStream)` after the comment that the API server reports failures there&#41;. A stream closed at creation cannot deliver the server&#39;s error text, so the `len(message) != 0` branch is dead and the code contradicts its own comment. client-go&#39;s `k8s.io/client-go/tools/portforward` keeps the error stream open for exactly this purpose.

**Trigger:** `DialLabRuntimeNodePort` &#40;or any library user&#41; forwarding to a pod port that is not listening. The API server closes the data stream and normally reports the reason on the error stream; here the client only sees EOF on the returned `net.Conn`.

**Impact:** Failed port-forwards fail silently, so users debugging a wrong port or a service that is not yet up get no explanation, and the error-reporting goroutine is dead code. The path is untested&#58; unit tests only exercise the upgrade-failure path before `CreateStream`, and the cluster robot test covers only the happy path. Whether apimachinery&#39;s SPDY `Stream.Close()` fully tears down the stream or half-closes it could not be verified from the snapshot, but either way the stated intent is not achieved.

**Suggested correction:** Keep the error stream open for the lifetime of the connection, mirroring client-go&#39;s portforward&#58; read it and, when a message arrives, close `remote` and surface the message &#40;at minimum to the log&#41;. Add a test that forwards to a closed port and asserts the failure is reported.


## P3 - New [`32-logs.robot`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/97a0b3b5da1ea93d0585c77987345c2adba9f81b/tests/01-smoke/32-logs.robot#L1-L1) suite is not matched by any CI workflow matrix

**Location:** [tests/01-smoke/32-logs.robot:1-91](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/97a0b3b5da1ea93d0585c77987345c2adba9f81b/tests/01-smoke/32-logs.robot#L1-L91)

**Problem:** The PR adds [`tests/01-smoke/32-logs.robot`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/97a0b3b5da1ea93d0585c77987345c2adba9f81b/tests/01-smoke/32-logs.robot#L1-L1), but [`.github/workflows/smoke-tests.yml`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/97a0b3b5da1ea93d0585c77987345c2adba9f81b/.github/workflows/smoke-tests.yml#L1-L1) is unchanged and its `test-suite` matrix ends at `"30*.robot"`; no other workflow references the suite. The pre-existing [`31-apply-network-mode.robot`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/97a0b3b5da1ea93d0585c77987345c2adba9f81b/tests/01-smoke/31-apply-network-mode.robot#L1-L1) shares the same gap, so the new suite extends an existing pattern.

**Trigger:** Every pull request&#58; the docker-runtime coverage the suite provides &#40;markers, `--tail`/`--timestamps`, follow, unknown-node rejection&#41; never runs.

**Impact:** The behavior this PR advertises for local runtimes has no CI enforcement, so regressions in the logs command would go unnoticed.

**Suggested correction:** Add `"32*.robot"` to the smoke-tests matrix &#40;and consider `"31*.robot"` for the sibling gap&#41;. Because [`rf-run.sh`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/97a0b3b5da1ea93d0585c77987345c2adba9f81b/tests/rf-run.sh#L1-L1) passes `--variable runtime:${runtime}` on the command line, which overrides the suite&#39;s own `docker` default, this also gives the podman job a shot at the logs path.


## Coverage

- All 37 changed paths were reviewed from the snapshot; both diffs and the corresponding head files were read, including callers of every new interface and the full identity plumbing &#40;`connect(req.Identity)` in all c9s methods, `Identity` on all request types in [`core/labruntime.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/97a0b3b5da1ea93d0585c77987345c2adba9f81b/core/labruntime.go#L1-L1), [`core/labruntime_access.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/97a0b3b5da1ea93d0585c77987345c2adba9f81b/core/labruntime_access.go#L1-L1), [`core/runtime_state.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/97a0b3b5da1ea93d0585c77987345c2adba9f81b/core/runtime_state.go#L1-L1), and [`core/events/stream.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/97a0b3b5da1ea93d0585c77987345c2adba9f81b/core/events/stream.go#L1-L1)&#41;.
- Nothing was executed&#58; Go unit tests, [`runtime/docker/logs_test.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/97a0b3b5da1ea93d0585c77987345c2adba9f81b/runtime/docker/logs_test.go#L1-L1), the robot suites, and `TestC9sClusterNodeAccess` were inspected, not run.
- The Podman bindings &#40;`go.podman.io/podman/v6 v6.1.4`&#41; and apimachinery SPDY sources are not present in the snapshot &#40;no vendor directory or module cache&#41;, so the newline behavior in finding 1 and the `errorStream.Close()` semantics in finding 2 are inferred, not verified from vendored code.
- The `metrics-server` version referenced by [`.github/workflows/clabernetes-tests.yml`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/97a0b3b5da1ea93d0585c77987345c2adba9f81b/.github/workflows/clabernetes-tests.yml#L1-L1) could not be verified offline.
- Checked and found sound&#58; podman&#39;s early-return drain goroutine &#40;no leak&#41;, Docker `WriteContainerLogs` TTY/stdcopy handling and context cancellation, `LogTail("all")` compatibility with Docker and Podman APIs, node-name matching for Docker via the `clab-node-name` label, and the impersonation test&#39;s RBAC setup in `14-clabernetes`.

1: ---
2: description: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring code to avoid overcomplication, make surgical changes, surface assumptions, and define verifiable success criteria.
3: alwaysApply: true
4: ---
5: 
6: # Karpathy behavioral guidelines
7: 
8: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Merge with project-specific instructions as needed.
9: 
10: **Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.
11: 
12: ## 1. Think Before Coding
13: 
14: **Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**
15: 
16: Before implementing:
17: 
18: - State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
19: - If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
20: - If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
21: - If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.
22: 
23: ## 2. Simplicity First
24: 
25: **Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**
26: 
27: - No features beyond what was asked.
28: - No abstractions for single-use code.
29: - No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
30: - No error handling for impossible scenarios.
31: - If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.
32: 
33: Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.
34: 
35: ## 3. Surgical Changes
36: 
37: **Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**
38: 
39: When editing existing code:
40: 
41: - Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
42: - Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
43: - Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
44: - If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.
45: 
46: When your changes create orphans:
47: 
48: - Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
49: - Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.
50: 
51: The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.
52: 
53: ## 4. Goal-Driven Execution
54: 
55: **Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**
56: 
57: Transform tasks into verifiable goals:
58: 
59: - "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
60: - "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
61: - "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"
62: 
63: For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:
64: 
65: ```
66: 1. [Step] → verify: [check]
67: 2. [Step] → verify: [check]
68: 3. [Step] → verify: [check]
69: ```
70: 
71: Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: **These guidelines are working if:** fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

(End of file - total 75 lines)
</content>

1: ---
2: description: Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode. Always pick the simplest solution that works.
3: globs:
4: alwaysApply: true
5: ---
6: 
7: # Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode
8: 
9: You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. The best code is the code never written.
10: 
11: Before writing any code, stop at the first rung that holds:
12: 
13: 1. Does this need to be built at all? (YAGNI)
14: 2. Does it already exist in this codebase? Reuse the helper, util, or pattern that's already here, don't re-write it.
15: 3. Does the standard library already do this? Use it.
16: 4. Does a native platform feature cover it? Use it.
17: 5. Does an already-installed dependency solve it? Use it.
18: 6. Can this be one line? Make it one line.
19: 7. Only then: write the minimum code that works.
20: 
21: The ladder runs after you understand the problem, not instead of it: read the task and the code it touches, trace the real flow end to end, then climb.
22: 
23: Bug fix = root cause, not symptom: a report names a symptom. Grep every caller of the function you touch and fix the shared function once — one guard there is a smaller diff than one per caller, and patching only the path the ticket names leaves a sibling caller still broken.
24: 
25: Rules:
26: 
27: - No abstractions that weren't explicitly requested.
28: - No new dependency if it can be avoided.
29: - No boilerplate nobody asked for.
30: - Deletion over addition. Boring over clever. Fewest files possible.
31: - Shortest working diff wins, but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
32: - Question complex requests: "Do you actually need X, or does Y cover it?"
33: - Pick the edge-case-correct option when two stdlib approaches are the same size, lazy means less code, not the flimsier algorithm.
34: - Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path.
35: 
36: Not lazy about: understanding the problem (read it fully and trace the real flow before picking a rung, a small diff you don't understand is just laziness dressed up as efficiency), input validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, the calibration real hardware needs (the platform is never the spec ideal, a clock drifts, a sensor reads off), anything explicitly requested. Lazy code without its check is unfinished: non-trivial logic leaves ONE runnable check behind, the smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks (an assert-based demo/self-check or one small test file; no frameworks, no fixtures). Trivial one-liners need no test.

(End of file - total 36 lines)
</content>

117: index 0000000..c1ee30b

120: @@ -0,0 +1,90 @@
121: +package cmd
122: +
123: +import (
124: +	"fmt"
125: +
126: +	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
127: +	clabcore "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/core"
128: +	clabutils "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/utils"
129: +)
130: +
131: +func logsCmd(o *Options) (*cobra.Command, error) {
132: +	c := &cobra.Command{
133: +		Use:   "logs",
134: +		Short: "show the logs of a lab node",
135: +		Long: "show the logs of a lab node's container, or of its device container with a lab " +
136: +			"runtime\nreference: https://containerlab.dev/cmd/logs/",
137: +		PreRunE: func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
138: +			if commandSkipsRoot(o.Global.Runtime) {
139: +				return nil
140: +			}
141: +
142: +			return clabutils.CheckAndGetRootPrivs()
143: +		},
144: +		SilenceUsage: true,
145: +		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
146: +			return logsFn(cmd, o)
147: +		},
148: +	}
149: +
150: +	c.Flags().StringVarP(
151: +		&o.Logs.Node,
152: +		"node",
153: +		"n",
154: +		o.Logs.Node,
155: +		"node to show the logs of",
156: +	)
157: +	c.Flags().Int64Var(
158: +		&o.Logs.Tail,
159: +		"tail",
160: +		o.Logs.Tail,
161: +		"number of lines to show from the end of the log; -1 shows the whole log",
162: +	)
163: +	c.Flags().BoolVarP(
164: +		&o.Logs.Follow,
165: +		"follow",
166: +		"f",
167: +		o.Logs.Follow,
168: +		"keep streaming new log lines",
169: +	)
170: +	c.Flags().BoolVar(
171: +		&o.Logs.Timestamps,
172: +		"timestamps",
173: +		o.Logs.Timestamps,
174: +		"prefix every line with its timestamp",
175: +	)
176: +
177: +	c.Example = `# Show the whole log of node srl1
178: +containerlab logs -t srl.clab.yml -n srl1
179: +
180: +# Follow the last 100 lines with timestamps
181: +containerlab logs --name srl -n srl1 --tail 100 --follow --timestamps`
182: +
183: +	return c, nil
184: +}
185: +
186: +func logsFn(cmd *cobra.Command, o *Options) error {
187: +	if o.Global.TopologyName == "" && o.Global.TopologyFile == "" {
188: +		return fmt.Errorf("provide either a lab name (--name) or a topology file path (--topo)")
189: +	}
190: +	if o.Logs.Node == "" {
191: +		return fmt.Errorf("provide the node to show the logs of (--node)")
192: +	}
193: +
194: +	c, err := clabcore.NewContainerLab(o.ToClabOptions()...)
195: +	if err != nil {
196: +		return err
197: +	}
198: +
199: +	opts := clabcore.NodeLogOptions{
200: +		NodeName:   o.Logs.Node,
201: +		Follow:     o.Logs.Follow,
202: +		Timestamps: o.Logs.Timestamps,
203: +	}
204: +	if o.Logs.Tail >= 0 {
205: +		tail := o.Logs.Tail
206: +		opts.Tail = &tail
207: +	}
208: +
209: +	return c.NodeLogs(cmd.Context(), opts, cmd.OutOrStdout(), cmd.ErrOrStderr())
210: +}

557: --- /dev/null

559: @@ -0,0 +1,246 @@
560: +package core
561: +
562: +import (
563: +	"context"
564: +	"fmt"
565: +	"io"
566: +	"net"
567: +	"sort"
568: +
569: +	clabconstants "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/constants"
570: +	clablabruntime "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/labruntime"
571: +	clabruntime "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/runtime"
572: +	clabtypes "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/types"
573: +)
574: +
575: +// The helpers in this file give library users per-node access to the lab selected by the CLab
576: +// (its topology file or WithTopologyName). Node names are accepted as the topology file spells
577: +// them or as a lab runtime sanitized them. Lab runtime calls act as the identity set with
578: +// WithLabRuntimeIdentity.
579: +
580: +// LocateLabRuntimeNodes reports the workload (namespace, pod, primary device container, Node
581: +// UID, exposed ports) of the given nodes, or of every node of the lab when none are given.
582: +func (c *CLab) LocateLabRuntimeNodes(
583: +	ctx context.Context,
584: +	nodeNames ...string,
585: +) ([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, error) {
586: +	locator, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeLocator](c, "locating nodes")
587: +	if err != nil {
588: +		return nil, err
589: +	}
590: +	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
591: +		return nil, err
592: +	}
593: +
594: +	return locator.LocateNode(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
595: +		Name:     c.Config.Name,
596: +		Nodes:    nodeNames,
597: +		Identity: c.labRuntimeIdentity,
598: +	})
599: +}
600: +
601: +// AttachLabRuntimeNode runs an interactive command in a node's device container (or in
602: +// req.Container) with stdin, an optional TTY and terminal resizing. The lab name and identity
603: +// default to the CLab's. A command exiting nonzero returns a *labruntime.CommandExitError.
604: +func (c *CLab) AttachLabRuntimeNode(
605: +	ctx context.Context,
606: +	req clablabruntime.AttachRequest,
607: +	streams clablabruntime.AttachStreams,
608: +) error {
609: +	attacher, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeAttacher](c, "attaching to nodes")
610: +	if err != nil {
611: +		return err
612: +	}
613: +
614: +	if req.Name == "" {
615: +		if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
616: +			return err
617: +		}
618: +		req.Name = c.Config.Name
619: +	}
620: +	if req.Identity.IsZero() {
621: +		req.Identity = c.labRuntimeIdentity
622: +	}
623: +
624: +	return attacher.Attach(ctx, req, streams)
625: +}
626: +
627: +// DialLabRuntimeNodePort opens a connection to a TCP port of a node (SSH, web UIs) through the
628: +// lab runtime, such as a Kubernetes port-forward.
629: +func (c *CLab) DialLabRuntimeNodePort(
630: +	ctx context.Context,
631: +	nodeName string,
632: +	port int,
633: +) (net.Conn, error) {
634: +	forwarder, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodePortForwarder](
635: +		c, "port-forwarding to nodes")
636: +	if err != nil {
637: +		return nil, err
638: +	}
639: +	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
640: +		return nil, err
641: +	}
642: +
643: +	return forwarder.DialPort(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
644: +		Name:     c.Config.Name,
645: +		Nodes:    []string{nodeName},
646: +		Identity: c.labRuntimeIdentity,
647: +	}, port)
648: +}
649: +
650: +// SampleLabRuntimeNodeStats reports the CPU and memory usage of the lab's running nodes. It
651: +// returns an error wrapping labruntime.ErrMetricsUnavailable when the cluster serves no resource
652: +// metrics.
653: +func (c *CLab) SampleLabRuntimeNodeStats(ctx context.Context) ([]clablabruntime.NodeStats, error) {
654: +	sampler, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeStatsSampler](
655: +		c, "sampling node stats")
656: +	if err != nil {
657: +		return nil, err
658: +	}
659: +	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
660: +		return nil, err
661: +	}
662: +
663: +	return sampler.SampleStats(ctx, clablabruntime.InspectRequest{
664: +		Name:     c.Config.Name,
665: +		Identity: c.labRuntimeIdentity,
666: +	})
667: +}
668: +
669: +// NodeLogOptions selects the node log NodeLogs writes.
670: +type NodeLogOptions struct {
671: +	// NodeName is the node whose log is written.
672: +	NodeName string
673: +	// Container overrides a lab runtime node's primary device container. Local runtimes do
674: +	// not support it.
675: +	Container string
676: +	// Tail limits the output to the last lines of the log; nil writes the whole log.
677: +	Tail *int64
678: +	// Follow keeps writing new log lines until the context ends.
679: +	Follow bool
680: +	// Timestamps prefixes every line with its timestamp.
681: +	Timestamps bool
682: +}
683: +
684: +// NodeLogs writes the log of a lab node with every runtime: the container log with Docker and
685: +// Podman, the device container log with a lab runtime. Lab runtimes write one combined stream to
686: +// stdout.
687: +func (c *CLab) NodeLogs(
688: +	ctx context.Context,
689: +	opts NodeLogOptions,
690: +	stdout, stderr io.Writer,
691: +) error {
692: +	if opts.NodeName == "" {
693: +		return fmt.Errorf("node name is required")
694: +	}
695: +	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
696: +		return err
697: +	}
698: +
699: +	if c.LabRuntime != nil {
700: +		streamer, err := labRuntimeCapability[clablabruntime.NodeLogStreamer](
701: +			c, "streaming node logs")
702: +		if err != nil {
703: +			return err
704: +		}
705: +
706: +		return streamer.StreamLogs(ctx, clablabruntime.LogRequest{
707: +			Name:       c.Config.Name,
708: +			NodeName:   opts.NodeName,
709: +			Container:  opts.Container,
710: +			Tail:       opts.Tail,
711: +			Follow:     opts.Follow,
712: +			Timestamps: opts.Timestamps,
713: +			Identity:   c.labRuntimeIdentity,
714: +		}, stdout)
715: +	}
716: +
717: +	if opts.Container != "" {
718: +		return fmt.Errorf("selecting a container is only supported with lab runtimes")
719: +	}
720: +
721: +	runtime, containerName, err := c.nodeContainer(ctx, opts.NodeName)
722: +	if err != nil {
723: +		return err
724: +	}
725: +
726: +	writer, ok := runtime.(clabruntime.ContainerLogWriter)
727: +	if !ok {
728: +		return fmt.Errorf("container runtime %q does not support node logs", runtime.GetName())
729: +	}
730: +
731: +	return writer.WriteContainerLogs(ctx, containerName, clabruntime.ContainerLogOptions{
732: +		Tail:       opts.Tail,
733: +		Follow:     opts.Follow,
734: +		Timestamps: opts.Timestamps,
735: +	}, stdout, stderr)
736: +}
737: +
738: +// nodeContainer finds the container of a lab node in the local container runtimes by the lab
739: +// and node name labels.
740: +func (c *CLab) nodeContainer(
741: +	ctx context.Context,
742: +	nodeName string,
743: +) (clabruntime.ContainerRuntime, string, error) {
744: +	filters := []*clabtypes.GenericFilter{
745: +		{
746: +			FilterType: "label",
747: +			Field:      clabconstants.Containerlab,
748: +			Operator:   "=",
749: +			Match:      c.Config.Name,
750: +		},
751: +		{
752: +			FilterType: "label",
753: +			Field:      clabconstants.NodeName,
754: +			Operator:   "=",
755: +			Match:      nodeName,
756: +		},
757: +	}
758: +
759: +	runtimeNames := make([]string, 0, len(c.Runtimes))
760: +	for name := range c.Runtimes {
761: +		runtimeNames = append(runtimeNames, name)
762: +	}
763: +	sort.Strings(runtimeNames)
764: +
765: +	for _, name := range runtimeNames {
766: +		runtime := c.Runtimes[name]
767: +
768: +		containers, err := runtime.ListContainers(ctx, filters)
769: +		if err != nil {
770: +			return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("could not list containers: %w", err)
771: +		}
772: +		if len(containers) != 0 && len(containers[0].Names) != 0 {
773: +			return runtime, containers[0].Names[0], nil
774: +		}
775: +	}
776: +
777: +	return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("%w: node %q of lab %q has no container",
778: +		ErrNodeNotFound, nodeName, c.Config.Name)
779: +}
780: +
781: +func (c *CLab) requireLabName() error {
782: +	if c.Config == nil || c.Config.Name == "" {
783: +		return fmt.Errorf("provide a lab name (--name) or a topology file (--topo)")
784: +	}
785: +
786: +	return nil
787: +}
788: +
789: +// labRuntimeCapability returns the CLab's lab runtime as an optional lab runtime interface.
790: +func labRuntimeCapability[T any](c *CLab, operation string) (T, error) {
791: +	var zero T
792: +
793: +	if c.LabRuntime == nil {
794: +		return zero, fmt.Errorf("%s needs a lab runtime such as %q",
795: +			operation, clablabruntime.ClabernetesRuntimeName)
796: +	}
797: +
798: +	capability, ok := c.LabRuntime.(T)
799: +	if !ok {
800: +		return zero, fmt.Errorf("lab runtime %q does not support %s",
801: +			c.globalRuntimeName, operation)
802: +	}
803: +
804: +	return capability, nil
805: +}

1031: +		func(_ context.Context, filters []*clabtypes.GenericFilter) (
1032: +			[]clabruntime.GenericContainer, error,
1033: +		) {

1035: +			for _, filter := range filters {

1038: +			if labels[clabconstants.Containerlab] != "lab1" {
1039: +				return nil, nil

1046: +		}).

1334: @@ -0,0 +1,57 @@
1335: +# logs command
1336: +
1337: +### Description
1338: +
1339: +The `logs` command shows the log of a lab node. With Docker and Podman it is the node container's log, with the [c9s runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#logs) the log of the node's primary device container in its pod.
1340: +
1341: +--8<-- "docs/cmd/deploy.md:env-vars-flags"
1342: +
1343: +### Usage
1344: +
1345: +`containerlab [global-flags] logs [local-flags]`
1346: +
1347: +### Flags
1348: +
1349: +#### topology | name
1350: +
1351: +Use the global `--topo | -t` flag to reference the lab topology file, or use the global `--name` flag to reference an already deployed lab by name. Without either, containerlab looks for a `*.clab.yml` file in the current directory, like the other lab commands.
1352: +
1353: +#### node
1354: +
1355: +Use the local `--node | -n` flag to select the node. The flag is required. With the c9s runtime the node name is accepted as the topology file spells it or as it was sanitized for Kubernetes (`R1` or `r1`).
1356: +
1357: +#### tail
1358: +
1359: +The local `--tail` flag limits the output to the last N lines of the log. The default `-1` shows the whole log; `--tail 0` shows no previous lines, which is useful with `--follow`.
1360: +
1361: +#### follow
1362: +
1363: +The local `--follow | -f` flag keeps streaming new log lines until the command is interrupted.
1364: +
1365: +#### timestamps
1366: +
1367: +The local `--timestamps` flag prefixes every line with its timestamp in RFC 3339 format.
1368: +
1369: +### Output
1370: +
1371: +The log goes to stdout. With Docker and Podman, the container's stderr goes to stderr, unless the container has a TTY; Kubernetes returns one combined stream, written to stdout.
1372: +
1373: +### Examples
1374: +
1375: +#### Show the whole log of a node
1376: +
1377: +```bash
1378: +containerlab logs -t srl.clab.yml -n srl1
1379: +```
1380: +
1381: +#### Follow the last 100 lines with timestamps
1382: +
1383: +```bash
1384: +containerlab logs --name srl -n srl1 --tail 100 --follow --timestamps
1385: +```
1386: +
1387: +#### Show the device log of a node in a c9s lab
1388: +
1389: +```bash
1390: +containerlab --runtime c9s logs --name clos -n srl1 --tail 50
1391: +```

1393: index 88e63a4..18dc015 100644
1394: --- a/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md
1395: +++ b/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md
1396: @@ -528,10 +528,24 @@ needs to reach the cluster.
1397:  If any selected command returns nonzero, or pod exec itself fails, the outer
1398:  `containerlab exec` also returns nonzero. Successful and failed results that
1399:  were received are still printed, so automation can use both the output and the
1400:  process exit status.
1401:  
1402: +## Logs
1403: +
1404: +`logs` shows the log of a node's primary device container, the same container
1405: +`exec` uses:
1406: +
1407: +```bash
1408: +containerlab --runtime c9s logs -t topo.clab.yml -n srl1
1409: +containerlab --runtime c9s logs --name clos -n srl1 --tail 100 --follow --timestamps
1410: +```
1411: +
1412: +It reads the `pods/log` subresource of the node's pod, so RBAC must allow
1413: +`get` on `pods/log`. Kubernetes returns stdout and stderr as one stream. See
1414: +the [`logs` command](../../cmd/logs.md) for the flags.
1415: +
1416:  ## Start, stop, and restart
1417:  
1418:  Node lifecycle commands operate on the kubernetes Deployments created by
1419:  Clabernetes.
1420:  
1421: @@ -782,10 +796,66 @@ token:
1422:  ```bash
1423:  kubectl -n <namespace> annotate node.c9s.run <node> \
1424:    c9s.run/device-state-reset=$(date +%s) --overwrite
1425:  ```
1426:  
1427: +## Node access from Go
1428: +
1429: +Programs that use containerlab as a Go library, such as clab-api-server, open
1430: +terminals, follow logs, reach node ports and read resource usage through
1431: +optional lab runtime interfaces in `github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/labruntime`,
1432: +implemented by the c9s runtime:
1433: +
1434: +| Interface | Method | What it does |
1435: +|---|---|---|
1436: +| `NodeLocator` | `LocateNode(ctx, NodeRequest) ([]NodeLocation, error)` | the namespace, pod, primary device container, Node UID, exposed ports and LoadBalancer address of nodes |
1437: +| `NodeAttacher` | `Attach(ctx, AttachRequest, AttachStreams) error` | an interactive exec with stdin, an optional TTY and a resize channel, in the device container or a chosen container |
1438: +| `NodeLogStreamer` | `StreamLogs(ctx, LogRequest, io.Writer) error` | the device container log, with tail, follow and timestamps |
1439: +| `NodePortForwarder` | `DialPort(ctx, NodeRequest, port) (net.Conn, error)` | a connection to a TCP port of the node's pod through `pods/portforward` (SSH, web UIs) |
1440: +| `NodeStatsSampler` | `SampleStats(ctx, InspectRequest) ([]NodeStats, error)` | CPU and memory per node from `metrics.k8s.io` PodMetrics, summing the node's device containers; without the metrics API the error wraps `labruntime.ErrMetricsUnavailable` |
1441: +
1442: +The `core` package wraps them per lab and node name, accepting the node name
1443: +as the topology file spells it or as it was sanitized:
1444: +`CLab.LocateLabRuntimeNodes`, `CLab.AttachLabRuntimeNode`,
1445: +`CLab.DialLabRuntimeNodePort`, `CLab.SampleLabRuntimeNodeStats` and
1446: +`CLab.NodeLogs`, which also serves Docker and Podman.
1447: +
1448: +```go
1449: +c, err := clabcore.NewContainerLab(
1450: +	clabcore.WithRuntime("c9s", nil),
1451: +	clabcore.WithTopologyName("clos"),
1452: +	clabcore.WithLabRuntimeIdentity(clablabruntime.Identity{
1453: +		User:   "clab:alice",
1454: +		Groups: []string{"clab:users"},
1455: +	}),
1456: +)
1457: +if err != nil {
1458: +	return err
1459: +}
1460: +
1461: +conn, err := c.DialLabRuntimeNodePort(ctx, "srl1", 22)
1462: +```
1463: +
1464: +### Acting as a user
1465: +
1466: +A server that runs labs for many users acts as each user, so the cluster's RBAC
1467: +decides what a user may do and its audit log names the user:
1468: +
1469: +- `labruntime.Identity{User, Groups}` is Kubernetes user impersonation.
1470: +  `labruntime.Config.Identity` sets it for a runtime, every request type has an
1471: +  `Identity` field that overrides it per call, and
1472: +  `clabcore.WithLabRuntimeIdentity` sets it for every call of a `CLab`.
1473: +- The c9s runtime builds one set of Kubernetes clients per identity from the
1474: +  kubeconfig and caches them. The impersonation applies to every transport:
1475: +  REST calls, watches, log streams, and the websocket and SPDY connections of
1476: +  exec, attach and port-forward.
1477: +- Without an identity, the kubeconfig is used as it is. The CLI has no
1478: +  impersonation flags: a CLI user acts with their own kubeconfig rights.
1479: +
1480: +The kubeconfig identity then needs the `impersonate` verb on the users and
1481: +groups it acts as.
1482: +
1483:  ## RBAC requirements
1484:  
1485:  The kube identity used by the outer containerlab process must be able to:
1486:  
1487:  - get, create, and delete namespaces when using automatic per-lab namespaces
1488: @@ -796,10 +866,13 @@ The kube identity used by the outer containerlab process must be able to:
1489:  - list and watch Pods
1490:  - list, get, and update Deployments
1491:  - create, get, list, update, and delete ConfigMaps used for local files
1492:  - exec into device Pods with `pods/exec`
1493:  - list and delete PersistentVolumeClaims for `destroy --cleanup`
1494: +- read container logs with `pods/log` for `logs`
1495: +- port-forward with `pods/portforward` for `NodePortForwarder`
1496: +- list `pods.metrics.k8s.io` for `NodeStatsSampler`
1497:  
1498:  Useful checks:
1499:  
1500:  ```bash
1501:  kubectl auth can-i get namespaces

With Docker and Podman it is the node container's log, with the [c9s runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#logs) the log of the node's primary device container in its pod.\n1340: +\n1341: +--8<-- \"docs/cmd/deploy.md:env-vars-flags\"\n1342: +\n1343: +### Usage\n1344: +\n1345: +`containerlab [global-flags] logs [local-flags]`\n1346: +\n1347: +### Flags\n1348: +\n1349: +#### topology | name\n1350: +\n1351: +Use the global `--topo | -t` flag to reference the lab topology file, or use the global `--name` flag to reference an already deployed lab by name. Without either, containerlab looks for a `*.clab.yml` file in the current directory, like the other lab commands.\n1352: +\n1353: +#### node\n1354: +\n1355: +Use the local `--node | -n` flag to select the node. The flag is required. With the c9s runtime the node name is accepted as the topology file spells it or as it was sanitized for Kubernetes (`R1` or `r1`).\n1356: +\n1357: +#### tail\n1358: +\n1359: +The local `--tail` flag limits the output to the last N lines of the log. The default `-1` shows the whole log; `--tail 0` shows no previous lines, which is useful with `--follow`.\n1360: +\n1361: +#### follow\n1362: +\n1363: +The local `--follow | -f` flag keeps streaming new log lines until the command is interrupted.\n1364: +\n1365: +#### timestamps\n1366: +\n1367: +The local `--timestamps` flag prefixes every line with its timestamp in RFC 3339 format.\n1368: +\n1369: +### Output\n1370: +\n1371: +The log goes to stdout. With Docker and Podman, the container's stderr goes to stderr, unless the container has a TTY; Kubernetes returns one combined stream, written to stdout.\n1372: +\n1373: +### Examples\n1374: +\n1375: +#### Show the whole log of a node\n1376: +\n1377: +```bash\n1378: +containerlab logs -t srl.clab.yml -n srl1\n1379: +```\n1380: +\n1381: +#### Follow the last 100 lines with timestamps\n1382: +\n1383: +```bash\n1384: +containerlab logs --name srl -n srl1 --tail 100 --follow --timestamps\n1385: +```\n1386: +\n1387: +#### Show the device log of a node in a c9s lab\n1388: +\n1389: +```bash\n1390: +containerlab --runtime c9s logs --name clos -n srl1 --tail 50\n1391: +```\n1392: diff --git a/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md b/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md\n1393: index 88e63a4..18dc015 100644\n1394: --- a/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md\n1395: +++ b/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md\n1396: @@ -528,10 +528,24 @@ needs to reach the cluster.\n1397:  If any selected command returns nonzero, or pod exec itself fails, the outer\n1398:  `containerlab exec` also returns nonzero. Successful and failed results that\n1399:  were received are still printed, so automation can use both the output and the\n1400:  process exit status.\n1401:  \n1402: +## Logs\n1403: +\n1404: +`logs` shows the log of a node's primary device container, the same container\n1405: +`exec` uses:\n1406: +\n1407: +```bash\n1408: +containerlab --runtime c9s logs -t topo.clab.yml -n srl1\n1409: +containerlab --runtime c9s logs --name clos -n srl1 --tail 100 --follow --timestamps\n1410: +```\n1411: +\n1412: +It reads the `pods/log` subresource of the node's pod, so RBAC must allow\n1413: +`get` on `pods/log`. Kubernetes returns stdout and stderr as one stream. See\n1414: +the [`logs` command](../../cmd/logs.md) for the flags.\n1415: +\n1416:  ## Start, stop, and restart\n1417:  \n1418:  Node lifecycle commands operate on the kubernetes Deployments created by\n1419:  Clabernetes.\n1420:  \n1421: @@ -782,10 +796,66 @@ token:\n1422:  ```bash\n1423:  kubectl -n <namespace> annotate node.c9s.run <node> \\\n1424:    c9s.run/device-state-reset=$(date +%s) --overwrite\n1425:  ```\n1426:  \n1427: +## Node access from Go\n1428: +\n1429: +Programs that use containerlab as a Go library, such as clab-api-server, open\n1430: +terminals, follow logs, reach node ports and read resource usage through\n1431: +optional lab runtime interfaces in `github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/labruntime`,\n1432: +implemented by the c9s runtime:\n1433: +\n1434: +| Interface | Method | What it does |\n1435: +|---|---|---|\n1436: +| `NodeLocator` | `LocateNode(ctx, NodeRequest) ([]NodeLocation, error)` | the namespace, pod, primary device container, Node UID, exposed ports and LoadBalancer address of nodes |\n1437: +| `NodeAttacher` | `Attach(ctx, AttachRequest, AttachStreams) error` | an interactive exec with stdin, an optional TTY and a resize channel, in the device container or a chosen container |\n1438: +| `NodeLogStreamer` | `StreamLogs(ctx, LogRequest, io.Writer) error` | the device container log, with tail, follow and timestamps |\n1439: +| `NodePortForwarder` | `DialPort(ctx, NodeRequest, port) (net.Conn, error)` | a connection to a TCP port of the node's pod through `pods/portforward` (SSH, web UIs) |\n1440: +| `NodeStatsSampler` | `SampleStats(ctx, InspectRequest) ([]NodeStats, error)` | CPU and memory per node from `metrics.k8s.io` PodMetrics, summing the node's device containers; without the metrics API the error wraps `labruntime.ErrMetricsUnavailable` |\n1441: +\n1442: +The `core` package wraps them per lab and node name, accepting the node name\n1443: +as the topology file spells it or as it was sanitized:\n1444: +`CLab.LocateLabRuntimeNodes`, `CLab.AttachLabRuntimeNode`,\n1445: +`CLab.DialLabRuntimeNodePort`, `CLab.SampleLabRuntimeNodeStats` and\n1446: +`CLab.NodeLogs`, which also serves Docker and Podman.\n1447: +\n1448: +```go\n1449: +c, err := clabcore.NewContainerLab(\n1450: +\tclabcore.WithRuntime(\"c9s\", nil),\n1451: +\tclabcore.WithTopologyName(\"clos\"),\n1452: +\tclabcore.WithLabRuntimeIdentity(clablabruntime.Identity{\n1453: +\t\tUser:   \"clab:alice\",\n1454: +\t\tGroups: []string{\"clab:users\"},\n1455: +\t}),\n1456: +)\n1457: +if err != nil {\n1458: +\treturn err\n1459: +}\n1460: +\n1461: +conn, err := c.DialLabRuntimeNodePort(ctx, \"srl1\", 22)\n1462: +```\n1463: +\n1464: +### Acting as a user\n1465: +\n1466: +A server that runs labs for many users acts as each user, so the cluster's RBAC\n1467: +decides what a user may do and its audit log names the user:\n1468: +\n1469: +- `labruntime.Identity{User, Groups}` is Kubernetes user impersonation.\n1470: +  `labruntime.Config.Identity` sets it for a runtime, every request type has an\n1471: +  `Identity` field that overrides it per call, and\n1472: +  `clabcore.WithLabRuntimeIdentity` sets it for every call of a `CLab`.\n1473: +- The c9s runtime builds one set of Kubernetes clients per identity from the\n1474: +  kubeconfig and caches them. The impersonation applies to every transport:\n1475: +  REST calls, watches, log streams, and the websocket and SPDY connections of\n1476: +  exec, attach and port-forward.\n1477: +- Without an identity, the kubeconfig is used as it is. The CLI has no\n1478: +  impersonation flags: a CLI user acts with their own kubeconfig rights.\n1479: +\n1480: +The kubeconfig identity then needs the `impersonate` verb on the users and\n1481: 1721: +	executor, err := r.newExecutor(execURL)
1722: +	if err != nil {
1723: +		return err
1724: +	}
1725: +
1726: +	options := remotecommand.StreamOptions{
1727: +		Stdin:  streams.Stdin,
1728: +		Stdout: streams.Stdout,
1729: +		Stderr: stderr,
1730: +		Tty:    req.TTY,
1731: +	}
1732: +	if req.TTY && streams.Resize != nil {
1733: +		options.TerminalSizeQueue = newTerminalSizeQueue(ctx, streams.Resize)
1734: +	}
1735: +
1736: +	err = executor.StreamWithContext(ctx, options)
1737: +
1738: +	var exitErr kubeexec.ExitError
1739: +	if errors.As(err, &exitErr) {
1740: +		return &clablabruntime.CommandExitError{Code: exitErr.ExitStatus()}
1741: +	}
1742: +	if err != nil {
1743: +		return fmt.Errorf("failed to attach to c9s node %s/%s/%s: %w",
1744: +			location.Namespace, req.Name, location.NodeName, err)
1745: +	}
1746: +
1747: +	return nil
1748: +}
1749: +
1750: +// newExecutor streams a pod exec over websockets, falling back to SPDY when the API server
1751: +// does not upgrade the websocket, like kubectl. The websocket executor reports upgrade
1752: +// failures with the k8s.io/streaming error types. Both transports are built from the runtime's
1753: +// rest config, so they carry its impersonation headers.
1754: +func (r *Runtime) newExecutor(execURL *url.URL) (remotecommand.Executor, error) {
1755: +	websocketExecutor, err := remotecommand.NewWebSocketExecutor(
1756: +		r.restConfig, http.MethodGet, execURL.String())
1757: +	if err != nil {
1758: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create Kubernetes websocket exec executor: %w", err)
1759: +	}
1760: +
1761: +	spdyExecutor, err := remotecommand.NewSPDYExecutor(r.restConfig, http.MethodPost, execURL)
1762: +	if err != nil {
1763: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create Kubernetes exec executor: %w", err)
1764: +	}
1765: +
1766: +	return remotecommand.NewFallbackExecutor(websocketExecutor, spdyExecutor,
1767: +		func(err error) bool {
1768: +			return streamhttp.IsUpgradeFailure(err) || streamhttp.IsHTTPSProxyError(err)
1769: +		})
1770: +}
1771: +
1772: +// terminalSizeQueue adapts a resize channel to the remotecommand size queue.
1773: +type terminalSizeQueue struct {
1774: +	ctx    context.Context
1775: +	resize <-chan clablabruntime.TerminalSize
1776: +}
1777: +
1778: +func newTerminalSizeQueue(
1779: +	ctx context.Context,
1780: +	resize <-chan clablabruntime.TerminalSize,
1781: +) *terminalSizeQueue {
1782: +	return &terminalSizeQueue{ctx: ctx, resize: resize}
1783: +}
1784: +
1785: +// Next blocks until the next size change; nil ends resizing.
1786: +func (q *terminalSizeQueue) Next() *remotecommand.TerminalSize {
1787: +	select {
1788: +	case <-q.ctx.Done():
1789: +		return nil
1790: +	case size, ok := <-q.resize:
1791: +		if !ok {
1792: +			return nil
1793: +		}
1794: +
1795: +		return &remotecommand.TerminalSize{Width: size.Width, Height: size.Height}
1796: +	}
1797: +}

1799: +// StreamLogs writes the log of a node's device container, or of the container the request
1800: +// names, to w.
1801: +func (r *Runtime) StreamLogs(
1802: +	ctx context.Context,
1803: +	req clablabruntime.LogRequest,
1804: +	w io.Writer,
1805: +) error {
1806: +	r, err := r.connect(req.Identity)
1807: +	if err != nil {
1808: +		return err
1809: +	}
1810: +
1811: +	location, err := r.runningNode(ctx, req.Name, req.Namespace, req.NodeName)
1812: +	if err != nil {
1813: +		return err
1814: +	}
1815: +
1816: +	container := req.Container
1817: +	if container == "" {
1818: +		container = location.Container
1819: +	}
1820: +
1821: +	stream, err := r.kubeClient.CoreV1().Pods(location.Namespace).
1822: +		GetLogs(location.Pod, &corev1.PodLogOptions{
1823: +			Container:  container,
1824: +			Follow:     req.Follow,
1825: +			Timestamps: req.Timestamps,
1826: +			TailLines:  req.Tail,
1827: +		}).Stream(ctx)
1828: +	if err != nil {
1829: +		return fmt.Errorf("failed to stream the log of c9s node %s/%s/%s: %w",
1830: +			location.Namespace, req.Name, location.NodeName, err)
1831: +	}
1832: +	defer stream.Close()
1833: +
1834: +	if _, err := io.Copy(w, stream); err != nil && ctx.Err() == nil {
1835: +		return fmt.Errorf("failed to stream the log of c9s node %s/%s/%s: %w",
1836: +			location.Namespace, req.Name, location.NodeName, err)
1837: +	}
1838: +
1839: +	return nil
1840: +}

1842: +// DialPort opens a connection to a TCP port of a node's pod through the Kubernetes port-forward
1843: +// subresource.
1844: +func (r *Runtime) DialPort(
1845: +	ctx context.Context,
1846: +	req clablabruntime.NodeRequest,
1847: +	port int,
1848: +) (net.Conn, error) {
1849: +	r, err := r.connect(req.Identity)
1850: +	if err != nil {
1851: +		return nil, err
1852: +	}
1853: +
1854: +	if len(req.Nodes) != 1 {
1855: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("port-forward needs exactly one node, got %d", len(req.Nodes))
1856: +	}
1857: +	if port <= 0 || port > 65535 {
1858: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid port %d", port)
1859: +	}
1860: +
1861: +	location, err := r.runningNode(ctx, req.Name, req.Namespace, req.Nodes[0])
1862: +	if err != nil {
1863: +		return nil, err
1864: +	}
1865: +
1866: +	conn, err := r.dialPodPort(location.Namespace, location.Pod, port)
1867: +	if err != nil {
1868: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to port-forward to port %d of c9s node %s/%s/%s: %w",
1869: +			port, location.Namespace, req.Name, location.NodeName, err)
1870: +	}
1871: +
1872: +	return conn, nil
1873: +}
1874: +
1875: +// dialPodPort opens a forwarded connection to a pod port over SPDY. The transport is built
1876: +// from the runtime's rest config, so it carries its impersonation headers.
1877: +func (r *Runtime) dialPodPort(namespace, pod string, port int) (net.Conn, error) {
1878: +	forwardURL := r.kubeClient.CoreV1().RESTClient().Post().
1879: +		Resource("pods").
1880: +		Name(pod).
1881: +		Namespace(namespace).
1882: +		SubResource("portforward").URL()
1883: +
1884: +	transport, upgrader, err := spdy.RoundTripperFor(r.restConfig)
1885: +	if err != nil {
1886: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create Kubernetes port-forward transport: %w", err)
1887: +	}
1888: +
1889: +	dialer := spdy.NewDialer(upgrader, &http.Client{Transport: transport}, http.MethodPost,
1890: +		forwardURL)
1891: +
1892: +	streamConn, _, err := dialer.Dial(portforward.PortForwardProtocolV1Name)
1893: +	if err != nil {
1894: +		return nil, err
1895: +	}
1896: +
1897: +	conn, err := newPortForwardConn(streamConn, port)
1898: +	if err != nil {
1899: +		_ = streamConn.Close()
1900: +
1901: +		return nil, err
1902: +	}
1903: +
1904: +	return conn, nil
1905: +}
1906: +
1907: +// newPortForwardConn opens the error and data streams of one forwarded connection and returns
1908: +// one end of an in-memory pipe whose other end is copied to and from the data stream. The pipe
1909: +// gives the caller a complete net.Conn, deadlines included.
1910: +func newPortForwardConn(streamConn httpstream.Connection, port int) (net.Conn, error) {
1911: +	requestID := strconv.FormatInt(portForwardRequestID.Add(1), 10)
1912: +
1913: +	headers := http.Header{}
1914: +	headers.Set(corev1.StreamType, corev1.StreamTypeError)
1915: +	headers.Set(corev1.PortHeader, strconv.Itoa(port))
1916: +	headers.Set(corev1.PortForwardRequestIDHeader, requestID)
1917: +
1918: +	errorStream, err := streamConn.CreateStream(headers)
1919: +	if err != nil {
1920: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create the error stream: %w", err)
1921: +	}
1922: +	// the client sends nothing on the error stream
1923: +	_ = errorStream.Close()
1924: +
1925: +	headers.Set(corev1.StreamType, corev1.StreamTypeData)
1926: +	dataStream, err := streamConn.CreateStream(headers)
1927: +	if err != nil {
1928: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create the data stream: %w", err)
1929: +	}
1930: +
1931: +	local, remote := net.Pipe()
1932: +
1933: +	var closeOnce sync.Once
1934: +	closeAll := func() {
1935: +		closeOnce.Do(func() {
1936: +			_ = remote.Close()
1937: +			_ = dataStream.Reset()
1938: +			_ = streamConn.Close()
1939: +		})
1940: +	}
1941: +
1942: +	go func() {
1943: +		// the API server reports a failure to reach the port on the error stream
1944: +		message, _ := io.ReadAll(errorStream)
1945: +		if len(message) != 0 {
1946: +			_ = remote.Close()
1947: +		}
1948: +	}()
1949: +
1950: +	go func() {
1951: +		defer closeAll()
1952: +		_, _ = io.Copy(remote, dataStream)
1953: +	}()
1954: +
1955: +	go func() {
1956: +		defer closeAll()
1957: +		_, _ = io.Copy(dataStream, remote)
1958: +	}()
1959: +
1960: +	go func() {
1961: +		<-streamConn.CloseChan()
1962: +		closeAll()
1963: +	}()
1964: +
1965: +	return local, nil
1966: +}

1968: +// SampleStats reports the CPU and memory usage of every running node of a lab from the
1969: +// resource metrics API, summing the node's device containers.
1970: +func (r *Runtime) SampleStats(
1971: +	ctx context.Context,
1972: +	req clablabruntime.InspectRequest,
1973: +) ([]clablabruntime.NodeStats, error) {
1974: +	r, err := r.connect(req.Identity)
1975: +	if err != nil {
1976: +		return nil, err
1977: +	}
1978: +
1979: +	state, err := r.Inspect(ctx, req)
1980: +	if err != nil {
1981: +		return nil, err
1982: +	}
1983: +
1984: +	metricsList, err := r.client.Resource(podMetricsGVR).Namespace(state.Namespace).
1985: +		List(ctx, metav1.ListOptions{})
1986: +	if err != nil {
1987: +		if apierrors.IsNotFound(err) || apierrors.IsServiceUnavailable(err) ||
1988: +			apierrors.IsMethodNotSupported(err) {
1989: +			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %v", clablabruntime.ErrMetricsUnavailable, err)
1990: +		}
1991: +
1992: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read pod metrics in namespace %s: %w",
1993: +			state.Namespace, err)
1994: +	}
1995: +
1996: +	metricsByPod := make(map[string]*unstructured.Unstructured, len(metricsList.Items))
1997: +	for idx := range metricsList.Items {
1998: +		metricsByPod[metricsList.Items[idx].GetName()] = &metricsList.Items[idx]
1999: +	}
2000: +
2001: +	deviceContainers, err := r.nodeDeviceContainers(ctx, state)
2002: +	if err != nil {
2003: +		return nil, err
2004: +	}
2005: +
2006: +	stats := make([]clablabruntime.NodeStats, 0, len(state.Nodes))
2007: +	for _, node := range state.Nodes {
2008: +		podMetrics := metricsByPod[node.Pod]
2009: +		if node.Pod == "" || podMetrics == nil {
2010: +			continue
2011: +		}
2012: +
2013: +		containers := deviceContainers[node.Name]
2014: +		if len(containers) == 0 && node.Container != "" {
2015: +			containers = map[string]bool{node.Container: true}
2016: +		}
2017: +
2018: +		sample, ok := podMetricsSample(podMetrics, containers)
2019: +		if !ok {
2020: +			continue
2021: +		}
2022: +
2023: +		sample.NodeName = node.Name
2024: +		sample.Namespace = state.Namespace
2025: +		sample.Pod = node.Pod
2026: +		stats = append(stats, sample)
2027: +	}
2028: +
2029: +	return stats, nil
2030: +}
2031: +
2032: +// nodeDeviceContainers reads the device containers of every node from its Node status.
2033: +func (r *Runtime) nodeDeviceContainers(
2034: +	ctx context.Context,
2035: +	state *clablabruntime.LabState,
2036: +) (map[string]map[string]bool, error) {
2037: +	nodes, err := r.nodesForTopology(ctx, state.Name, state.Namespace)
2038: +	if err != nil {
2039: +		return nil, err
2040: +	}
2041: +
2042: +	result := make(map[string]map[string]bool, len(nodes.Items))
2043: +	for idx := range nodes.Items {
2044: +		directContainers, _, _ := unstructured.NestedSlice(
2045: +			nodes.Items[idx].Object, "status", "directContainers")
2046: +
2047: +		names := map[string]bool{}
2048: +		for _, raw := range directContainers {
2049: +			entry, ok := raw.(map[string]any)
2050: +			if !ok {
2051: +				continue
2052: +			}
2053: +			if name, _ := entry["name"].(string); name != "" {
2054: +				names[name] = true
2055: +			}
2056: +		}
2057: +		result[nodes.Items[idx].GetName()] = names
2058: +	}
2059: +
2060: +	return result, nil
2061: +}
2062: +
2063: +// podMetricsSample sums the usage of the given containers of a PodMetrics object.
2064: +func podMetricsSample(
2065: +	podMetrics *unstructured.Unstructured,
2066: +	containers map[string]bool,
2067: +) (clablabruntime.NodeStats, bool) {
2068: +	rawContainers, _, _ := unstructured.NestedSlice(podMetrics.Object, "containers")
2069: +
2070: +	var (
2071: +		cpu    resource.Quantity
2072: +		memory resource.Quantity
2073: +		found  bool
2074: +	)
2075: +	for _, raw := range rawContainers {
2076: +		entry, ok := raw.(map[string]any)
2077: +		if !ok {
2078: +			continue
2079: +		}
2080: +		name, _ := entry["name"].(string)
2081: +		if !containers[name] {
2082: +			continue
2083: +		}
2084: +
2085: +		usage, _ := entry["usage"].(map[string]any)
2086: +		if value, ok := usage["cpu"].(string); ok {
2087: +			if quantity, err := resource.ParseQuantity(value); err == nil {
2088: +				cpu.Add(quantity)
2089: +			}
2090: +		}
2091: +		if value, ok := usage["memory"].(string); ok {
2092: +			if quantity, err := resource.ParseQuantity(value); err == nil {
2093: +				memory.Add(quantity)
2094: +			}
2095: +		}
2096: +		found = true
2097: +	}
2098: +	if !found {
2099: +		return clablabruntime.NodeStats{}, false
2100: +	}
2101: +
2102: +	sample := clablabruntime.NodeStats{
2103: +		CPUMilliCores: cpu.MilliValue(),
2104: +		MemoryBytes:   memory.Value(),
2105: +	}
2106: +	if value, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(podMetrics.Object, "timestamp"); value != "" {
2107: +		sample.Timestamp, _ = time.Parse(time.RFC3339, value)
2108: +	}
2109: +	if value, _, _ := unstructured.NestedString(podMetrics.Object, "window"); value != "" {
2110: +		sample.Window, _ = time.ParseDuration(value)
2111: +	}
2112: +
2113: +	return sample, true
2114: +}

2298: +func podMetrics(name string, containers map[string][2]string) *unstructured.Unstructured {
2299: +	entries := make([]any, 0, len(containers))
2300: +	for container, usage := range containers {
2301: +		entries = append(entries, map[string]any{
2302: +			"name":  container,
2303: +			"usage": map[string]any{"cpu": usage[0], "memory": usage[1]},
2304: +		})
2305: +	}
2306: +
2307: +	return &unstructured.Unstructured{Object: map[string]any{
2308: +		"apiVersion": "metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1",
2309: +		"kind":       "PodMetrics",
2310: +		"metadata":   map[string]any{"name": name, "namespace": "lab-ns"},
2311: +		"timestamp":  "2026-10-27T10:00:00Z",
2312: +		"window":     "15s",
2313: +		"containers": entries,
2314: +	}}
2315: +}

2370: +func TestTerminalSizeQueue(t *testing.T) {
2371: +	t.Parallel()
2372: +
2373: +	resize := make(chan clablabruntime.TerminalSize, 1)
2374: +	queue := newTerminalSizeQueue(context.Background(), resize)
2375: +
2376: +	resize <- clablabruntime.TerminalSize{Width: 120, Height: 40}
2377: +	if size := queue.Next(); size == nil || size.Width != 120 || size.Height != 40 {
2378: +		t.Fatalf("Next() = %+v", size)
2379: +	}
2380: +
2381: +	close(resize)
2382: +	if size := queue.Next(); size != nil {
2383: +		t.Fatalf("Next() after close = %+v, want nil", size)
2384: +	}
2385: +
2386: +	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
2387: +	cancel()
2388: +	if size := newTerminalSizeQueue(
2389: +		ctx,
2390: +		make(chan clablabruntime.TerminalSize),
2391: +	).Next(); size != nil {
2392: +		t.Fatalf("Next() after cancel = %+v, want nil", size)
2393: +	}
2394: +}

2396: +// impersonationRecorder is an API server stub that records the impersonation headers of every
2397: +// request and answers with a Status error.
2398: +type impersonationRecorder struct {
2399: +	mu       sync.Mutex
2400: +	requests []recordedRequest
2401: +}
2402: +
2403: +type recordedRequest struct {
2404: +	method string
2405: +	path   string
2406: +	user   string
2407: +	groups []string
2408: +}
2409: +
2410: +func (rec *impersonationRecorder) ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request) {
2411: +	rec.mu.Lock()
2412: +	rec.requests = append(rec.requests, recordedRequest{
2413: +		method: req.Method,
2414: +		path:   req.URL.Path,
2415: +		user:   req.Header.Get("Impersonate-User"),
2416: +		groups: req.Header.Values("Impersonate-Group"),
2417: +	})
2418: +	rec.mu.Unlock()
2419: +
2420: +	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
2421: +	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusForbidden)
2422: +	_, _ = io.WriteString(w,
2423: +		`{"kind":"Status","apiVersion":"v1","status":"Failure","reason":"Forbidden","code":403}`)
2424: +}
2425: +
2426: +func (rec *impersonationRecorder) take() []recordedRequest {
2427: +	rec.mu.Lock()
2428: +	defer rec.mu.Unlock()
2429: +
2430: +	requests := rec.requests
2431: +	rec.requests = nil
2432: +
2433: +	return requests
2434: +}
2435: +
2436: +func TestIdentityImpersonatesOnEveryTransport(t *testing.T) {
2437: +	t.Parallel()
2438: +
2439: +	recorder := &impersonationRecorder{}
2440: +	server := httptest.NewServer(recorder)
2441: +	defer server.Close()
2442: +
2443: +	r := &Runtime{
2444: +		identity: clablabruntime.Identity{User: "clab:default"},
2445: +		clients: &clientLoader{
2446: +			loadConfig: func() (*rest.Config, string, error) {
2447: +				return &rest.Config{Host: server.URL}, "", nil
2448: +			},
2449: +			newClients: newKubeClients,
2450: +		},
2451: +	}
2452: +	alice := clablabruntime.Identity{
2453: +		User:   "clab:alice",
2454: +		Groups: []string{"clab:users", "clab:admins"},
2455: +	}
2456: +
2457: +	view, err := r.connect(alice)
2458: +	if err != nil {
2459: +		t.Fatal(err)
2460: +	}
2461: +	again, err := r.connect(alice)
2462: +	if err != nil || again.kubeClient != view.kubeClient {
2463: +		t.Fatal("clients of one identity were not cached")
2464: +	}
2465: +	defaultView, err := r.connect(clablabruntime.Identity{})
2466: +	if err != nil || defaultView.kubeClient == view.kubeClient {
2467: +		t.Fatal("the configured identity shares the clients of another identity")
2468: +	}
2469: +
2470: +	ctx := context.Background()
2471: +	pod := &corev1.Pod{ObjectMeta: metav1.ObjectMeta{Name: "lab1-r1-abc", Namespace: "lab-ns"}}
2472: +
2473: +	// REST
2474: +	_, _ = r.Inspect(ctx, clablabruntime.InspectRequest{Name: "lab1", Identity: alice})
2475: +	// pod exec: websocket first, then SPDY
2476: +	_, _, _, _ = view.execInPod(ctx, pod, "node-r1-x", []string{"true"})
2477: +	// port-forward over SPDY
2478: +	if conn, err := view.dialPodPort("lab-ns", "lab1-r1-abc", 22); err == nil {
2479: +		_ = conn.Close()
2480: +	}
2481: +	// a call without identity uses the configured one
2482: +	_, _ = r.Inspect(ctx, clablabruntime.InspectRequest{Name: "lab1"})
2483: +
2484: +	requests := recorder.take()
2485: +	seen := map[string]bool{}
2486: +	for _, req := range requests {
2487: +		switch {
2488: +		case strings.HasSuffix(req.path, "/exec"):
2489: +			seen["exec-"+req.method] = true
2490: +		case strings.HasSuffix(req.path, "/portforward"):
2491: +			seen["portforward"] = true
2492: +		default:
2493: +			seen["rest-"+req.user] = true
2494: +		}
2495: +
2496: +		if req.user == "clab:default" {
2497: +			if len(req.groups) != 0 {
2498: +				t.Fatalf("configured identity sent groups: %+v", req)
2499: +			}
2500: +			continue
2501: +		}
2502: +		if req.user != alice.User || strings.Join(req.groups, ",") != "clab:users,clab:admins" {
2503: +			t.Fatalf("request without alice's impersonation: %+v", req)
2504: +		}
2505: +	}
2506: +
2507: +	for _, want := range []string{
2508: +		"rest-clab:alice", "exec-GET", "exec-POST", "portforward", "rest-clab:default",
2509: +	} {
2510: +		if !seen[want] {
2511: +			t.Fatalf("no %s request recorded: %+v", want, requests)
2512: +		}
2513: +	}
2514: +}

184: // applyLabRuntimeDefaultTimeout gives remote, controller-driven lab runtimes enough time to load

187: func applyLabRuntimeDefaultTimeout(cobraCmd *cobra.Command, o *Options) {
188: 	if !clablabruntime.IsLabRuntimeName(o.Global.Runtime) {
189: 		return

198: 		return
199: 	}

249: func checkLabRuntimeCommandSupport(cobraCmd *cobra.Command, runtimeName string) error {
250: 	if !clablabruntime.IsLabRuntimeName(runtimeName) {
251: 		return nil
252: 	}
253: 
254: 	for cmd := cobraCmd; cmd != nil; cmd = cmd.Parent() {
255: 		if _, ok := labRuntimeUnsupportedCommands[cmd.Name()]; ok {
256: 			return fmt.Errorf("the %q command is not supported with lab runtime %q",
257: 				cmd.Name(), runtimeName)
258: 		}
259: 	}
260: 
261: 	if getCommandPath(cobraCmd) == "graph" && !graphRendersFromTopologyFile(cobraCmd) {
262: 		return fmt.Errorf(
263: 			"the %q command needs running containers with lab runtime %q unless it renders "+
264: 				"from the topology file alone; use --offline, --dot, --mermaid or --drawio",
265: 			"graph", runtimeName)
266: 	}
267: 
268: 	if getCommandPath(cobraCmd) == "inspect.interfaces" {
269: 		return fmt.Errorf("the %q command is not supported with lab runtime %q",
270: 			"inspect interfaces", runtimeName)
271: 	}
272: 
273: 	var unsupported []string
274: 	for _, flagName := range labRuntimeUnsupportedFlags[getCommandPath(cobraCmd)] {
275: 		if labRuntimeFlagWasSet(cobraCmd, flagName) {
276: 			unsupported = append(unsupported, "--"+flagName)
277: 		}
278: 	}
279: 	if len(unsupported) != 0 {
280: 		sort.Strings(unsupported)
281: 
282: 		return fmt.Errorf(
283: 			"flag(s) %s are not supported with the %q command and lab runtime %q",
284: 			strings.Join(unsupported, ", "),
285: 			cobraCmd.Name(),
286: 			runtimeName,
287: 		)
288: 	}
289: 
290: 	return nil
291: }

293: func graphRendersFromTopologyFile(cobraCmd *cobra.Command) bool {
294: 	for _, flagName := range graphTopologyFileFlags {
295: 		flag := cobraCmd.Flag(flagName)
296: 		if flag != nil && flag.Value.String() == "true" &&
297: 			labRuntimeFlagWasSet(cobraCmd, flagName) {
298: 			return true
299: 		}
300: 	}
301: 
302: 	return false
303: }
304: 
305: func labRuntimeFlagWasSet(cobraCmd *cobra.Command, flagName string) bool {
306: 	flag := cobraCmd.Flag(flagName)
307: 	if flag == nil {
308: 		return false
309: 	}
310: 
311: 	if flag.Changed {
312: 		return true
313: 	}
314: 
315: 	if v == nil {
316: 		return false
317: 	}
318: 
319: 	commandKey := getCommandPath(cobraCmd) + "." + flagName
320: 	if v.IsSet(commandKey) {
321: 		return true
322: 	}
323: 
324: 	return v.IsSet(flagName)
325: }

327: // getTopoFilePath finds *.clab.y*ml file in the current working directory
328: // if the file was not specified.
329: // If the topology file refers to a git repository, it will be cloned to the current directory.
330: // Errors if more than one file is found by the glob path.
331: func getTopoFilePath(cobraCmd *cobra.Command, o *Options) error { // skipcq: GO-R1005
332: 	// set commands which may use topo file find functionality, the rest don't need it
333: 	if cobraCmd.Name() != "deploy" &&
334: 		cobraCmd.Name() != "destroy" &&
335: 		cobraCmd.Name() != "start" &&
336: 		cobraCmd.Name() != "stop" &&
337: 		cobraCmd.Name() != "restart" &&
338: 		cobraCmd.Name() != "redeploy" &&
339: 		cobraCmd.Name() != "inspect" &&
340: 		cobraCmd.Name() != "save" &&
341: 		cobraCmd.Name() != "graph" &&
342: 		cobraCmd.Name() != "validate" &&
343: 		cobraCmd.Name() != "logs" &&
344: 		cobraCmd.Name() != "interfaces" {
345: 		return nil
346: 	}
347: 
348: 	// start/stop/restart topology lookup applies only to top-level lifecycle commands.
349: 	// nested commands like tools api-server start|stop are excluded.
350: 	if (cobraCmd.Name() == "start" || cobraCmd.Name() == "stop" || cobraCmd.Name() == "restart") &&
351: 		(cobraCmd.Parent() == nil || cobraCmd.Parent().Name() != "containerlab") {
352: 		return nil
353: 	}
354: 
355: 	// inspect and destroy commands with --all flag don't use file find functionality
356: 	if (cobraCmd.Name() == "inspect" || cobraCmd.Name() == "destroy") &&
357: 		cobraCmd.Flag("all") != nil &&
358: 		cobraCmd.Flag("all").Value.String() == "true" {
359: 		return nil
360: 	}
361: 
362: 	var err error
363: 	// perform topology clone/fetch if the topo file is not available locally
364: 	if !clabutils.FileOrDirExists(o.Global.TopologyFile) {
365: 		switch {
366: 		case clabgit.IsGitHubOrGitLabURL(o.Global.TopologyFile) ||
367: 			clabgit.IsGitHubShortURL(o.Global.TopologyFile):
368: 			o.Global.TopologyFile, err = processGitTopoFile(o.Global.TopologyFile)
369: 			if err != nil {
370: 				return err
371: 			}
372: 		case clabutils.IsHttpURL(o.Global.TopologyFile, true):
373: 			// canonize the passed topo as URL by adding https schema if it was missing
374: 			if !strings.HasPrefix(o.Global.TopologyFile, "http://") &&
375: 				!strings.HasPrefix(o.Global.TopologyFile, "https://") {
376: 				o.Global.TopologyFile = "https://" + o.Global.TopologyFile
377: 			}
378: 		}
379: 	}
380: 
381: 	// if topo or name flags have been provided, don't try to derive the topo file
382: 	if o.Global.TopologyFile != "" || o.Global.TopologyName != "" {
383: 		return nil
384: 	}
385: 
386: 	log.Debugf("trying to find topology files automatically")
387: 
388: 	files, err := filepath.Glob("*.clab.y*ml")
389: 
390: 	if len(files) == 0 {
391: 		return errors.New("no topology files matching the pattern *.clab.yml or *.clab.yaml found")
392: 	}
393: 
394: 	if len(files) > 1 {
395: 		if !term.IsTerminal(os.Stdin.Fd()) {
396: 			return fmt.Errorf(
397: 				"more than one topology file matching the pattern *.clab.yml or *.clab.yaml found, "+
398: 					"can't pick one: %q",
399: 				files,
400: 			)
401: 		}
402: 
403: 		running := runningTopoFiles(cobraCmd.Context(), o)
404: 
405: 		selected, err := selectTopoFile(files, running)
406: 		if err != nil {
407: 			return err
408: 		}
409: 
410: 		o.Global.TopologyFile = selected
411: 
412: 		log.Info("Using topology file", "file", selected)
413: 
414: 		return nil
415: 	}
416: 
417: 	o.Global.TopologyFile = files[0]
418: 
419: 	log.Debugf("topology file found: %s", files[0])
420: 
421: 	return err
422: }

424: func processGitTopoFile(topo string) (string, error) {
425: 	// for short github urls, prepend https://github.com
426: 	// note that short notation only works for github links
427: 	if clabgit.IsGitHubShortURL(topo) {
428: 		topo = "https://github.com/" + topo
429: 	}
430: 
431: 	repo, err := clabgit.NewRepo(topo)
432: 	if err != nil {
433: 		return "", err
434: 	}
435: 
436: 	// Instantiate the git implementation to use.
437: 	gitImpl := clabgit.NewGoGit(repo)
438: 
439: 	// clone the repo via the Git Implementation
440: 	err = gitImpl.Clone()
441: 	if err != nil {
442: 		return "", err
443: 	}
444: 
445: 	// adjust permissions for the checked out repo
446: 	// it would belong to root/root otherwise
447: 	err = clabutils.SetUIDAndGID(repo.GetName())
448: 	if err != nil {
449: 		log.Errorf("error adjusting repository permissions %v. Continuing anyways", err)
450: 	}
451: 
452: 	// prepare the path with the repo based path
453: 	path := filepath.Join(repo.GetPath()...)
454: 	// prepend that path with the repo base directory
455: 	path = filepath.Join(repo.GetName(), path)
456: 
457: 	// change dir to the
458: 	err = os.Chdir(path)
459: 	if err != nil {
460: 		return "", err
461: 	}
462: 
463: 	return repo.GetFilename(), err
464: }

53: 	Resource: "nodes",
54: }

57: 	Group:    "c9s.run",
58: 	Version:  "v1alpha1",
59: 	Resource: "links",
60: }
61: 
62: var nodeProfileGVR = schema.GroupVersionResource{

67: 
68: type Runtime struct {
69: 	client     dynamic.Interface
70: 	kubeClient kubernetes.Interface
71: 	restConfig *rest.Config
72: 	namespace  string
73: 	// labNamespaceOverride is set by --namespace or CLAB_KUBE_NAMESPACE. When
74: 	// empty, lab-scoped operations derive their namespace from the lab name.
75: 	labNamespaceOverride string
76: 	timeout              time.Duration
77: 	// kindLinkApplyMode resolves the default link apply mode a node kind declares.
78: 	// The plan uses it to predict the pod lifecycle impact of link changes.
79: 	kindLinkApplyMode func(kind string) string
80: 	// clients loads the Kubernetes clients on first use. Commands that only compile the
81: 	// topology (validate, deploy --emit-crs) never call it, so they work without a
82: 	// kubeconfig that loads. It is nil when the clients were injected (tests).
83: 	clients *clientLoader
84: 	// connected marks a runtime view whose client fields are populated.
85: 	connected bool
86: 	// identity is the configured identity of calls without one; in a connected view it is the
87: 	// identity the clients impersonate.
88: 	identity clablabruntime.Identity
89: }
90: 
91: // kubeClients is the set of Kubernetes clients a runtime view operates with.
92: type kubeClients struct {
93: 	dynamic    dynamic.Interface
94: 	kube       kubernetes.Interface
95: 	restConfig *rest.Config
96: }
97: 
98: // clientLoader loads the kubeconfig once and builds, and caches, the Kubernetes clients of
99: // every identity from it.
100: type clientLoader struct {
101: 	loadConfig func() (*rest.Config, string, error)
102: 	newClients func(*rest.Config) (*kubeClients, error)
103: 
104: 	once      sync.Once
105: 	base      *rest.Config
106: 	namespace string
107: 	err       error
108: 
109: 	mu         sync.Mutex
110: 	byIdentity map[string]*kubeClients
111: }
112: 
113: func newClientLoader() *clientLoader {
114: 	return &clientLoader{
115: 		loadConfig: kubeClientConfig,
116: 		newClients: newKubeClients,
117: 	}
118: }
119: 
120: func newKubeClients(restConfig *rest.Config) (*kubeClients, error) {
121: 	client, err := dynamic.NewForConfig(restConfig)
122: 	if err != nil {
123: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create Kubernetes dynamic client: %w", err)
124: 	}
125: 
126: 	kubeClient, err := kubernetes.NewForConfig(restConfig)
127: 	if err != nil {
128: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create Kubernetes client: %w", err)
129: 	}
130: 
131: 	return &kubeClients{dynamic: client, kube: kubeClient, restConfig: restConfig}, nil
132: }
133: 
134: // load returns the clients of an identity. The impersonation is part of the rest config, so it
135: // applies to every transport built from it: REST calls, watches, log streams, and the SPDY and
136: // websocket upgrades of exec, attach and port-forward.
137: func (l *clientLoader) load(
138: 	identity clablabruntime.Identity,
139: ) (*kubeClients, string, error) {
140: 	l.once.Do(func() {
141: 		l.base, l.namespace, l.err = l.loadConfig()
142: 		if l.namespace == "" {
143: 			l.namespace = defaultNamespace
144: 		}
145: 	})
146: 	if l.err != nil {
147: 		return nil, "", l.err
148: 	}
149: 
150: 	key := identityKey(identity)
151: 
152: 	l.mu.Lock()
153: 	defer l.mu.Unlock()
154: 
155: 	if clients, ok := l.byIdentity[key]; ok {
156: 		return clients, l.namespace, nil
157: 	}
158: 
159: 	restConfig := rest.CopyConfig(l.base)
160: 	if !identity.IsZero() {
161: 		restConfig.Impersonate = rest.ImpersonationConfig{
162: 			UserName: identity.User,
163: 			Groups:   slices.Clone(identity.Groups),
164: 		}
165: 	}
166: 
167: 	clients, err := l.newClients(restConfig)
168: 	if err != nil {
169: 		return nil, "", err
170: 	}
171: 	if l.byIdentity == nil {
172: 		l.byIdentity = map[string]*kubeClients{}
173: 	}
174: 	l.byIdentity[key] = clients
175: 
176: 	return clients, l.namespace, nil
177: }
178: 
179: func identityKey(identity clablabruntime.Identity) string {
180: 	return identity.User + "\x00" + strings.Join(identity.Groups, "\x00")
181: }
182: 
183: // connect returns a view of the runtime with the Kubernetes clients of an identity populated,
184: // loading the kubeconfig on first use. A zero identity uses the runtime's configured identity.
185: // Every operation that reads or changes cluster state calls it first.
186: func (r *Runtime) connect(identity clablabruntime.Identity) (*Runtime, error) {
187: 	if identity.IsZero() {
188: 		identity = r.identity
189: 	}
190: 	if r.connected && identity.Equal(r.identity) {
191: 		return r, nil
192: 	}
193: 	if r.clients == nil {
194: 		// clients were injected (tests); they act as the identity they were built with
195: 		return r, nil
196: 	}
197: 
198: 	clients, namespace, err := r.clients.load(identity)
199: 	if err != nil {
200: 		return nil, err
201: 	}
202: 
203: 	view := *r
204: 	view.client = clients.dynamic
205: 	view.kubeClient = clients.kube
206: 	view.restConfig = clients.restConfig
207: 	if view.namespace == "" {
208: 		view.namespace = namespace
209: 	}
210: 	view.identity = identity
211: 	view.connected = true
212: 
213: 	return &view, nil
214: }
215: 
216: func withKubernetesClientDebugLogs(ctx context.Context) context.Context {
217: 	verbosity := -1
218: 	if log.GetLevel() <= log.DebugLevel {
219: 		verbosity = 3
220: 	}
221: 	logger := funcr.New(func(prefix, args string) {
222: 		log.Debug("Kubernetes client", "log", strings.TrimSpace(prefix+" "+args))
223: 	}, funcr.Options{Verbosity: verbosity})
224: 
225: 	return klog.NewContext(ctx, logger)
226: }
227: 
228: func init() {
229: 	clablabruntime.Register(clablabruntime.ClabernetesRuntimeName, New)
230: }
231: 
232: // New returns the c9s lab runtime. It does not load the kubeconfig: the Kubernetes clients
233: // are created on the first operation that needs the cluster.
234: func New(cfg clablabruntime.Config) (clablabruntime.LabRuntime, error) {
235: 	return &Runtime{
236: 		labNamespaceOverride: configuredLabNamespace(cfg.Namespace),
237: 		timeout:              cfg.Timeout,
238: 		kindLinkApplyMode:    cfg.KindLinkApplyMode,
239: 		identity:             cfg.Identity,
240: 		clients:              newClientLoader(),
241: 	}, nil
242: }

The impersonation is part of the rest config, so it\n// applies to every transport built from it: REST calls, watches, log streams, and the SPDY and\n// websocket upgrades of exec, attach and port-forward.\nfunc (l *clientLoader) load(\n\tidentity clablabruntime.Identity,\n) (*kubeClients, string, error) {\n\tl.once.Do(func() {\n\t\tl.base, l.namespace, l.err = l.loadConfig()\n\t\tif l.namespace == \"\" {\n\t\t\tl.namespace = defaultNamespace\n\t\t}\n\t})\n\tif l.err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, \"\", l.err\n\t}\n\n\tkey := identityKey(identity)\n\n\tl.mu.Lock()\n\tdefer l.mu.Unlock()\n\n\tif clients, ok := l.byIdentity[key]; ok {\n\t\treturn clients, l.namespace, nil\n\t}\n\n\trestConfig := rest.CopyConfig(l.base)\n\tif !identity.IsZero() {\n\t\trestConfig.Impersonate = rest.ImpersonationConfig{\n\t\t\tUserName: identity.User,\n\t\t\tGroups:   slices.Clone(identity.Groups),\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tclients, err := l.newClients(restConfig)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, \"\", err\n\t}\n\tif l.byIdentity == nil {\n\t\tl.byIdentity = map[string]*kubeClients{}\n\t}\n\tl.byIdentity[key] = clients\n\n\treturn clients, l.namespace, nil\n}\n\nfunc identityKey(identity clablabruntime.Identity) string {\n\treturn identity.User + \"\\x00\" + strings.Join(identity.Groups, \"\\x00\")\n}\n\n// connect returns a view of the runtime with the Kubernetes clients of an identity populated,\n// loading the kubeconfig on first use. A zero identity uses the runtime's configured identity.\n// Every operation that reads or changes cluster state calls it first.\nfunc (r *Runtime) connect(identity clablabruntime.Identity) (*Runtime, error) {\n\tif identity.IsZero() {\n\t\tidentity = r.identity\n\t}\n\tif r.connected && identity.Equal(r.identity) {\n\t\treturn r, nil\n\t}\n\tif r.clients == nil {\n\t\t// clients were injected (tests); they act as the identity they were built with\n\t\treturn r, nil\n\t}\n\n\tclients, namespace, err := r.clients.load(identity)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\n\tview := *r\n\tview.client = clients.dynamic\n\tview.kubeClient = clients.kube\n\tview.restConfig = clients.restConfig\n\tif view.namespace == \"\" {\n\t\tview.namespace = namespace\n\t}\n\tview.identity = identity\n\tview.connected = true\n\n\treturn &view, nil\n}\n\nfunc withKubernetesClientDebugLogs(ctx context.Context) context.Context {\n\tverbosity := -1\n\tif log.GetLevel() <= log.DebugLevel {\n\t\tverbosity = 3\n\t}\n\tlogger := funcr.New(func(prefix, args string) {\n\t\tlog.Debug(\"Kubernetes client\", \"log\", strings.TrimSpace(prefix+\" \"+args))\n\t}, funcr.Options{Verbosity: verbosity})\n\n\treturn klog.NewContext(ctx, logger)\n}\n\nfunc init() {\n\tclablabruntime.Register(clablabruntime.ClabernetesRuntimeName, New)\n}\n\n// New returns the c9s lab runtime. It does not load the kubeconfig: the Kubernetes clients\n// are created on the first operation that needs the cluster.\nfunc New(cfg clablabruntime.Config) (clablabruntime.LabRuntime, error) {\n\treturn &Runtime{\n\t\tlabNamespaceOverride: configuredLabNamespace(cfg.Namespace),\n\t\ttimeout:              cfg.Timeout,\n\t\tkindLinkApplyMode:    cfg.KindLinkApplyMode,\n\t\tidentity:             cfg.Identity,\n\t\tclients:              newClientLoader(),\n\t}, nil\n}",

45: // LocateNode reports the pod, primary device container, Node UID and exposed ports of the
46: // requested nodes, or of every node of the lab when the request names none. Node names are
47: // accepted as the topology or as the cluster spells them.
48: func (r *Runtime) LocateNode(
49: 	ctx context.Context,
50: 	req clablabruntime.NodeRequest,
51: ) ([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, error) {
52: 	r, err := r.connect(req.Identity)
53: 	if err != nil {
54: 		return nil, err
55: 	}
56: 
57: 	state, err := r.Inspect(ctx, clablabruntime.InspectRequest{
58: 		Name:      req.Name,
59: 		Namespace: req.Namespace,
60: 	})
61: 	if err != nil {
62: 		return nil, err
63: 	}
64: 
65: 	nodes := make(map[string]clablabruntime.NodeState, len(state.Nodes))
66: 	for _, node := range state.Nodes {
67: 		nodes[node.Name] = node
68: 	}
69: 
70: 	if len(req.Nodes) == 0 {
71: 		locations := make([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, 0, len(state.Nodes))
72: 		for _, node := range state.Nodes {
73: 			locations = append(locations, nodeLocation(state, node))
74: 		}
75: 
76: 		return locations, nil
77: 	}
78: 
79: 	locations := make([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, 0, len(req.Nodes))
80: 	for _, nodeName := range req.Nodes {
81: 		resolved, ok := resolveKnownNodeName(nodes, nodeName)
82: 		if !ok {
83: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("node %q was not found in c9s lab %s/%s",
84: 				nodeName, state.Namespace, state.Name)
85: 		}
86: 		locations = append(locations, nodeLocation(state, nodes[resolved]))
87: 	}
88: 
89: 	return locations, nil
90: }
91: 
92: func nodeLocation(
93: 	state *clablabruntime.LabState,
94: 	node clablabruntime.NodeState,
95: ) clablabruntime.NodeLocation {
96: 	return clablabruntime.NodeLocation{
97: 		NodeName:            node.Name,
98: 		Namespace:           state.Namespace,
99: 		Pod:                 node.Pod,
100: 		Container:           node.Container,
101: 		NodeUID:             node.NodeUID,
102: 		ExposedPorts:        node.ExposedPorts,
103: 		LoadBalancerAddress: node.LoadBalancerAddress,
104: 	}
105: }

107: // runningNode locates one node and requires it to have a pod and a device container.
108: func (r *Runtime) runningNode(
109: 	ctx context.Context,
110: 	lab,
111: 	namespace,
112: 	nodeName string,
113: ) (clablabruntime.NodeLocation, error) {
114: 	if lab == "" {
115: 		return clablabruntime.NodeLocation{}, fmt.Errorf("topology name is required")
116: 	}
117: 	if nodeName == "" {
118: 		return clablabruntime.NodeLocation{}, fmt.Errorf("node name is required")
119: 	}
120: 
121: 	locations, err := r.LocateNode(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
122: 		Name:      lab,
123: 		Namespace: namespace,
124: 		Nodes:     []string{nodeName},
125: 	})
126: 	if err != nil {
127: 		return clablabruntime.NodeLocation{}, err
128: 	}
129: 
130: 	location := locations[0]
131: 	if location.Pod == "" {
132: 		return clablabruntime.NodeLocation{}, fmt.Errorf(
133: 			"c9s node %s/%s/%s has no pod; is it running?",
134: 			location.Namespace, lab, location.NodeName)
135: 	}
136: 
137: 	return location, nil
138: }
